summary: Sends the X11 §8 byte-order + MAJOR/MINOR probe and reads status. status=1 -> unauthenticated display. Very tight, correct T1 today - the server accepted the setup (nearly a T2 already). Biggest gap: doesn't follow through with a QueryTree/GetGeometry/GetImage to render a proof-of-access screenshot; doesn't feed a loot artifact. No coverage for the write-only cookie families or MIT-MAGIC-COOKIE guessing.

findings.tier_evidence: Server returned status=Success (1) to a no-cookie handshake - the server itself accepted the connection setup, no auth needed. This is stronger than most T1 findings; it's the doorstep of T2.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow the accepted setup with GetGeometry(root) + GetImage on a tiny 8x8 region and save the pixmap. Proves live framebuffer read, not just handshake ack. Screenshot via xwd is a T3-shaped tester_next_step but the T2 in-module is the pixel read.
findings.tester_next_step: DISPLAY=<ip>:<display> xwd -root -out /tmp/scr.xwd && convert /tmp/scr.xwd /tmp/scr.png; then DISPLAY=<ip>:<display> xdotool key ctrl+alt+t   # spawn a terminal on the target's live desktop

findings.tier_evidence: Handshake refused with status=0 - port speaks X but access-controlled. Discovery only.
findings.promotion_notes: Try a small set of common cookie material (empty MIT-MAGIC-COOKIE-1, all-zeros, sniffed local cookies) - a hit promotes to full T2. Also try XDMCP query on UDP/177 - some setups pair open XDMCP with an xhost-restricted 6000.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -sU -p 177 --script xdmcp-discover <ip>; and: DISPLAY=<ip>:<display> xhost + 2>&1   # test if the operator left xhost + on at some point
